blogs.title: Choking on Air: When Dysphagia Is Neurologic, Not ENT
blogs.description: Equal difficulty with solids and liquids plus normal laryngoscopy/endoscopy should pivot you away from GERD/structural ENT causes toward brainstem pathology. We review neurogenic dysphagia patterns in Chiari I, bedside clues of lower cranial nerve involvement, and when to order brain/cervical MRI despite multiple normal scopes.

blogs.title: The Silent Desaturator: Central Hypoventilation Without Dyspnea in Chiari I
blogs.description: Profound, unperceived hypoxemia isn’t always anxiety—think impaired brainstem interoception and acquired Ondine’s curse. We unpack why patients can ‘forget to breathe’ without air hunger, monitoring strategies (prioritize capnography), and immediate ED/clinic pitfalls that miss life-threatening events.

blogs.title: Read the Old Films: The Crowded Foramen Magnum You Already Have
blogs.description: A 14-year-old ‘normal’ head CT hid a crowded foramen magnum. This post shows what to ask radiology to re-review (craniocervical junction, CSF spaces, tonsillar position), why CT can miss functional crowding, and when historical imaging reinterpretation changes today’s workup.

blogs.title: AHI Lies (Sometimes): How Type III Studies Underestimate Central Events
blogs.description: A ‘mild’ AHI can be dangerously misleading when EEG is missing. We explain why Type III polysomnography dilutes event rates with wake time, how to interpret a high central-event fraction, and when to escalate to full PSG with CO2 monitoring in suspected brainstem disease.

blogs.title: Voluntary vs Automatic Breathing: Bedside Clues to Acquired Ondine’s Curse
blogs.description: Normal daytime ABGs with episodic desats during distraction or sleep signal preserved voluntary but impaired automatic drive. Learn the clinical phenotype, precipitants, and how to structure observation and monitoring to catch failures of automatic respiration early.

blogs.title: Decompress or Don’t? Navigating Surgery vs NIV in Chiari-Related Respiratory Failure
blogs.description: Posterior fossa decompression can reverse central events, but timing and patient preference matter. We outline who needs urgent neurosurgical evaluation, when to trial CPAP/BiPAP/ASV, how to monitor nonoperatively, and red flags that should tip the balance toward surgery.

blogs.title: The Haircut That Helped: Atypical Headache and Scalp Allodynia in Chiari I
blogs.description: Not all Chiari headaches are cough/Valsalva. We discuss vertex allodynia, nummular-like pain, and occipital neuralgia mimics that derail diagnosis. Practical takeaways for history-taking that broaden your index of suspicion when ‘typical’ Chiari features are absent.

blogs.title: ED Playbook: Sedation, Oxygen, and Airway in Suspected Central Hypoventilation
blogs.description: Opioids/benzodiazepines can unmask catastrophic hypoventilation in brainstem compression. We cover safe analgesia/sedation choices, continuous capnography, targeted oxygenation, when to use NIV, and intubation pearls (maintain normocapnia, mindful neck positioning) while you hunt for a structural cause.

blogs.title: Post-Trauma Chiari: Unmasking vs Causing—What Clinicians Should Do
blogs.description: Symptoms after minor head injury may reflect either acquired tonsillar descent or revelation of a previously silent Chiari. We provide a pragmatic algorithm: who to image (new occipital headaches, dysphagia, sleep-disordered breathing), what sequences to order, and how to counsel patients amid etiologic uncertainty.
